rv.q: This is one issue with this entertaining but rocky new revival
Overall, this iteration feels like a production at an arts-based middle school, which isn't a bad thing.
The staging isn't much better or worse than any of the thousands of other amateur productions of 'Charlie Brown.'
You'll be charmed, I'm sure, if you go see this show.
This entertaining revival has the novelty of being performed by a cast of lively professional child performers.
The endearing young performers providing oomph are irresistible.
This 'Charlie Brown' should have great appeal to the small set who will discover or rediscover simple life lessons and the wonders of Peanuts characters.
It might have been an enjoyable afternoon but the show did not live up to its potential.
In trying to literalize Schulz's world, Unger and company have killed the joke.
